__NOTOC__
The dictionary in La Bangu project contains definitions of words in Simple English and simplified dialects of local languages.

In particular in [[jbovlaste]] it reuses Simple English direction for English speakers.

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheet/ccc?key=0Ahngu1CNj7wddEljb0o5YzkzSU4zVXhtam5CUGMzZkE#gid=7 The current 'Lojban-Simple English' dictionary for La Bangu]. <!--Prepared for translation into other languages with English as the source of translation.-->

==Simple English==
Simple English doesn't have much common with Wikipedia's Simple English, Ogden's Basic English or Simple Technical English. It tries to present gimste in simple wordage and thus more usable for beginners in Lojban.

==Changes from official definitions==
*The order or places is mostly the same as in official definitions so you don't have to relearn.
* However, there are a few changes when the corpus of Lojbanic texts strongly suggests the need in a change and/or leads to misusage. Some of those changes are:
** the third place of '''traji3''' is taken from the fourth place
** '''mabla''', '''zabna''', '''satci''', '''konju''' change their place structure
*Not mentioning "by standard" places for most (but not all) {{jvs|smuvelcki}} where they exist. Only less than 25 "by standard" places and 4 "under conditions" places retained and are to be rephrased.
*Some place are ignored. Not using places is equivalent to '''zi'o''' or '''zo'e''' depending on context. If a place is used in a discourse next usage oof the same selbri without this place assumes that this place is filled with '''zo'e'''='''lo co'e'''.
* Strictly specifying what sumti ([[noun]]) type can be accepted in each te sumti (place of a [[verb]]).
**roles of tersumti are specified when necessary
**If several sumti types are possible for the same place all of them are mentioned. '''No other sumti types is possible for this place.''' This allows to better understand the place structure.
*Clearly specifying sumti interactions like in gua\spi language (e.g. "property of x2" place)

==Changes in lexicon==
* Some BAI are removed (marked as "deprecated" in "jargon" field, not included into basic lists).
* UI get new definitions approved by [[User:Robin Lee Powell|camgusmis]].
* 

==Morphology==
Types of words:
# basic brivla: fu'ivla, cimjvo, gismu, cmevla
## cimjvo are considered non-decomposable.
## fu'ivla might get regularized suffixes (thus they would belong to compound brivla) specifying their semantic classes. Thus ideologically they are like rafsi-suffixes (idea by [[la selpa'i]])
# compound brivla: jvajvo.
## jvajvo are taught separately from cimjvo
## in jvajvo CVV rafsi can act only as suffixes.
## CCV rafsi can go anywhere.
## CVC rafsi are deleted ('''retsku''' is no different from fu'ivla, but '''retskugau''' has the -gau suffix).
==Te sumti types==
*event (traditionally uses '''nu''') or proposition (traditionally uses '''du'u''').
*topic
*property
*text
*number

===Additional orthogonal types===
* set of other types
* ordered set of other types
* realis/irrealis of a place by default. See [[ELG: Subjunctives in detail#Global subjunctivity|Global subjunctivity]]
The dictionary specifies if set or ordered set of any sumti types or particular sumti types is possible for each place of the verb.

==Raising, lowering rules. Te sumti types interactions==
#no place can be both ''topic'' and ''event/proposition/property''
#if we have event selbri and event sumti they match. No raising. '''mi djica lo se nitcu'''
#if we have event selbri and topic sumti then raising is assumed. '''mi lerci''', '''mi djica lo plise''', '''lo mlatu cu melbi'''
#if we have topic selbri and event sumti then lowering (add '''kantu''') is assumed
